name: Shimri
title: A Benjaminite warrior who joined David
summary: Shimri was a Benjaminite who joined David while he was in Ziklag, fleeing from King Saul. He was among the brave warriors who came to David and supported him before he became king over all Israel. The name Shimri means 'The Lord preserves' and also appears among those who had taken foreign wives in Ezra's time.

keyEvents.title: Joins David at Ziklag
keyEvents.description: Shimri was one of the Benjaminites who came to David at Ziklag while he still had to stay away from Saul, son of Kish. These warriors were skilled with both right and left hands in slinging stones and shooting arrows with a bow.

keyEvents.title: David's Growing Army
keyEvents.description: Shimri was part of an ever-growing group of skilled warriors who came to David, so that his camp became as large as God's camp.

keyEvents.title: The Benjaminites' Shift of Loyalty
keyEvents.description: It was remarkable that Benjaminites like Shimri left Saul's tribe to support David, showing God's guidance in gathering support for the coming king.

keyEvents.title: Namesake in Ezra's Time
keyEvents.description: Another man named Shimri is mentioned among those who had taken foreign wives and had to separate from them after returning from exile in Babylon, in accordance with Ezra's reform.
